pr.title: feat(products): cache product pages in Redis and invalidate on edit

flows.name: Read: product page through the cache
flows.summary: A product page read now tries Redis first and only falls through to Postgres on a miss. Check that the cache key carries everything the response varies on, or two shoppers can be served each other's page.

steps.title: Request the product
steps.note: Unchanged: the page fetches `GET /products/:id` with the shopper's currency in the `Accept-Currency` header.

steps.title: Build the cache key
steps.note: The key is `product:{id}:{currency}`. Currency is in it because prices are converted server-side; locale is not, because copy is translated in the browser.

steps.title: Look the page up
steps.note: A `GET` on the key. A Redis error is logged and treated as a miss, so an outage degrades to the old uncached path instead of a 500.

steps.title: Load from the database
steps.note: Unchanged query: the product, its variants and the converted price in one round trip.

steps.title: Fill the cache
steps.note: `SET` with a 10 minute TTL. The TTL is the backstop for any write path that forgets to invalidate; the edit flow is the primary way entries leave.

steps.title: Return the page
steps.note: Sets `X-Cache: hit|miss` so the hit rate shows up in the access logs without new metrics.

flows.name: Write: an edit invalidates the cache
flows.summary: Saving a product deletes its cached pages after the transaction commits, then queues a warm-up. The order is the thing to check: invalidating before the commit lets a concurrent read refill the cache with the old row.

steps.title: Handle the edit
steps.note: Wraps the write in a transaction and registers the invalidation as an after-commit hook rather than calling it inline.

steps.title: Write the row
steps.note: Unchanged `UPDATE`. The after-commit hook only fires if this commits; a rollback leaves the cache alone.

steps.title: Delete every currency's entry
steps.note: `SCAN` for `product:{id}:*` and `DEL` the matches. One key per currency, so a single delete would miss most of them.

steps.title: Warm-up job queued
steps.note: A job on the existing background queue, so the edit returns without waiting for the cache to refill.

steps.title: Re-render the default currency
steps.note: Refills only the store's default currency; the rest fill on first read. The job runner itself landed separately.
